A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from EDP to ExDM. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original Maze2d exploration, URLB fine-tuning and ablation results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original seven-maze exploration, Gaussian and diffusion policy fine-tuning, and ablation results.

M1.justification: In v1, the conditional action diffusion policy supplies the intrinsic reward Rscore(s,a). v2 Section 3.1 and Algorithm 1 add a separate state diffusion model and derive Rscore(s) from state modeling while retaining action modeling. Section 3.2 also introduces Gaussian-policy fine-tuning alongside the retained IQL/CEP diffusion procedure.

E1.justification: Maze coverage expands from Square-b, Square-c and Square-tree to include Square-a, Square-d, Square-bottleneck and Square-large. This extends evaluation to bottlenecked and substantially more complex maze geometries. The four URLB domains and their sixteen downstream tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The maze comparison expands beyond RND, DIAYN and BeCL to include ICM, Disagreement, LBS, SMM, LSD, CIC and CeSD. URLB adds CeSD and a separate diffusion fine-tuning comparison against DQL, IDQL, QSM and DIPO. CeSD was already cited in v1 but was not evaluated there.

E3.justification: Maze pre-training changes from 500k to 100k steps. v2 separately evaluates Gaussian-policy fine-tuning with DDPG and diffusion-policy fine-tuning, and introduces pre-training budgets of 100k, 500k, 1M and 2M steps for sensitivity analysis. Standard URLB budgets of 2M pre-training and 100k fine-tuning steps remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds aggregate and per-domain pre-training-duration analyses in Figures 6(a) and 11. It removes v1's score-reward ablation and the direct comparison between replay-buffer trajectories and samples from pre-trained policies in Figures 3, 8 and 9. Q-learning and diffusion sampling-step analyses are retained in v2 Figures 6(b–c).

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports Maze2d means and standard deviations over ten seeds in Table 1; v1's maze plots show bands without specifying the maze seed count or uncertainty definition. URLB retains ten seeds per task and stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. The added disclosure does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive maze results and separate Gaussian/diffusion fine-tuning results; Table 4 reports Gaussian-policy IQM of 0.80 for ExDM versus 0.71 for CeSD. Retained baseline values also change: CIC's Jaco top-right score changes from 168.9 to 167.6, and BeCL's Quadruped walk score from 640.3 to 694.9. Proposed-method scores involve changed methods and policy settings, so they are not direct same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.1, deriving a geometric-probability bound concerning nondeterministic maximum-state-entropy policies under an assumption of independent, uniformly distributed deterministic-policy state occupancies. The earlier policy-improvement and convergence theorem is retained as Theorem 3.2 with its proof in Appendix A.2.

C1.justification: The contribution is reframed from an exploratory diffusion policy supplying rewards and downstream initialization to a diffusion-model framework supporting both Gaussian and diffusion adaptation. Performance claims broaden from beating exploration methods and competing with skill-based methods to outperforming URL and diffusion fine-tuning baselines, with particular emphasis on complicated mazes.

C2.justification: v2 Section 5.4 newly reports that diffusion-policy fine-tuning underperforms Gaussian-policy fine-tuning and tentatively attributes this to limited online interactions, qualifying the earlier emphasis on diffusion-policy initialization. Section 5.6 adds explicit limitations concerning discrete actions and computational costs. The pre-training explanation also shifts toward maximizing state entropy.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix C.3 and Table 2 newly disclose extensive DDPG and diffusion hyperparameters, architectures and optimization details. Appendices C.1 and C.7 add episode limits, hardware and training times; C.2 adds implementation sources for new baselines. These are substantial documentation additions, not evidence that previously unspecified settings changed. Both versions state that code is in supplementary material.

R1.justification: The URL and diffusion-RL literature framing remains, with expanded citations including DIME, Soft Diffusion Actor-Critic, EUCLID and geometric-probability work. General language-model and vision pre-training references are removed. The novelty positioning is broadened from diffusion policies for unsupervised exploration to diffusion models in URL, without replacing the central research positioning.

P1.justification: The EDP-to-ExDM renaming accompanies extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, pre-training explanation and experimental narrative. Experiments now distinguish Gaussian and diffusion fine-tuning, appendices are reorganized, and Broader Impact moves from the main text to Appendix D.

P2.justification: The main text switches from two columns to one. Conceptual diagrams are redrawn and combined into v2 Figure 1; maze plots and trajectory panels are substantially reorganized; ablations are combined into Figure 6. New coverage, hyperparameter and aggregate-results tables and URLB task illustrations materially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: v2 separates Gaussian-policy/DDPG evaluation from diffusion-policy fine-tuning comparisons, reducing v1's confounding of exploration and policy-class advantages. Relevant new comparators and challenging maze evaluations strengthen the evidence, while explicit hyperparameters and computing details substantially improve reproducibility. Removing the score-reward and direct policy-diversity ablations weakens component attribution, and the new theorem relies on idealized assumptions, but the evaluation and reproducibility gains provide a substantial net improvement.
